part.deflection.title: Deflection
part.deflection.summary: A forcing move pulls the defender away from its post, and the piece it guarded is left loose; first, find the right defender.
ex.df.kylSr: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.df.kylSr.hint: The black rook on c7 is attacked by your rook on c3. Count its defenders.
ex.df.kylSr.solution: 53.Rd1+! The check hits the king on d6, the only defender of the rook on c7. After 53...Ke5 the king leaves the file, and 54.Rxc7 captures the rook.
ex.df.V9Ggd: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.df.V9Ggd.hint: Count the defenders of the bishop on f6, which your queen attacks.
ex.df.V9Ggd.solution: 32.h6+! The pawn gives check, and the king, the only defender of the bishop on f6, has to leave g7. After 32...Kxh6, 33.Qxf6 captures the bishop.
ex.df.1yuX7: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.df.1yuX7.hint: Your bishop attacks the knight on e4. Count its defenders.
ex.df.1yuX7.solution: 35...Rd3+! The rook gives check, and the king on f3, the only defender of the knight on e4, has to move. After 36.Ke2, 36...Bxe4, and the bishop defends the rook the king attacks.
ex.df.AZu96: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.df.AZu96.hint: Count the defenders of the black queen on e4.
ex.df.AZu96.solution: 45.Rf8+! The rook gives check, and the rook on e8 has to capture it: the bishop on h6 watches f8. With the rook gone from the e-file, 45...Rxf8 46.Qxe4.
ex.df.yhrkM: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.df.yhrkM.hint: Count the defenders of the white queen on c2.
ex.df.yhrkM.solution: 28...Ra1+! The rook gives check on the first rank. If 29.Rb1, the rook on b2 leaves the queen undefended, and 29...Qxc2. If 29.Ke2, 29...Re1 is mate. And if 29.Bd1, 29...Qxc2 also wins material.
ex.df.w24bQ: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.df.w24bQ.hint: Count the defenders of the white rook on c1.
ex.df.w24bQ.solution: 26...e3+! The pawn gives check, and the king on d2, the only defender of the rook on c1, has to move: d1 and c2 are watched by the bishop on a4. After 27.Kxe3, 27...Rxc1.
ex.df.yVwet: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.df.yVwet.hint: See who defends the queen on d3 and look for a check that also attacks the queen and forces that defender to capture.
ex.df.yVwet.solution: 32...Nf2+! The knight gives check and attacks the queen on d3: it is a fork. If 33.Rxf2, the rook on d2, the only defender of the queen, leaves its post, and 33...Qxd3 captures it.
ex.df.A0ceO: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.df.A0ceO.hint: See who defends the rook on f3 and look for a move that attacks that defender and the rook at once.
ex.df.A0ceO.solution: 30.Nd4+! The knight gives check and attacks the rook on f3: it is a fork. The king on e2, the only defender of the rook, has to move, and after 30...Kd2, 31.Rxf3 captures it.
part.attraction.title: Attraction
part.attraction.summary: A piece given up pulls the king to a square where the blow awaits it; first, check which piece will capture.
ex.at.PUKqj: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.at.PUKqj.hint: The white king is on the h-file. Look for the piece to give up that pulls it to a square where your other rook gives mate.
ex.at.PUKqj.solution: 33...Rxh5+! The rook captures the pawn with check, and the king can only capture it. After 34.Kxh5, 34...Rh8 is mate: your king on f5 takes g4, g5 and g6.
ex.at.wYrLB: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.at.wYrLB.hint: Look for the check that gives up a piece and leads the black king to a square where your queen gives mate.
ex.at.wYrLB.solution: 33.Rxh6+! The rook captures the pawn with check, and the king has to capture it. After 33...Kxh6, 34.Qg6 is mate: the pawn on h5 defends the queen, and the rook on f5 watches g5.
ex.at.0J1BO: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.at.0J1BO.hint: Look for the check that gives up a piece and leads the black king to a square where your queen gives mate.
ex.at.0J1BO.solution: 33.Rxc8+! The rook captures the rook with check, and the king has to capture it. After 33...Kxc8, 34.Qc7 is mate: the knight on e6 defends the queen.
ex.at.ZTLdR: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.at.ZTLdR.hint: Look for the check that gives up a piece and leads the white king to a square where your rook gives mate.
ex.at.ZTLdR.solution: 23...Qxg1+! The queen captures the rook with check, and the king has to capture it. After 24.Kxg1, 24...Rf1 is mate: the bishop on e2 defends the rook.
ex.at.C1Hz0: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.at.C1Hz0.hint: Look for the check that gives up a piece and brings the black king forward, where your queen gives mate.
ex.at.C1Hz0.solution: 19.Bxf7+! The bishop captures the pawn with check, and the king has to capture it. After 19...Kxf7, 20.Qe6 is mate: the bishop on g7 watches f8 and defends the pawn on f6.
ex.at.ODY6I: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.at.ODY6I.hint: Find the square where the black king would be within reach of your knight together with the queen on d7.
ex.at.ODY6I.solution: 30.Rxg8+! The rook captures the knight with check, and the king has to capture it. After 30...Kxg8, 31.Nxf6+ is a fork: the knight gives check and attacks the queen on d7.
ex.at.zdWY1: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.at.zdWY1.hint: Look for the check that gives up a piece and leads the black king to a square where your rook gives mate.
ex.at.zdWY1.solution: 26.Qxh7+! The queen captures the knight with check, and the king has to capture it. After 26...Kxh7, 27.Rh6 is mate: the knight on f5 defends the rook and watches g7.
ex.at.OWmTi: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.at.OWmTi.hint: Look for the check that gives up a piece and leads the black king to a square where your queen gives mate.
ex.at.OWmTi.solution: 31.Rh8+! The rook gives check, and the king has to capture it: the knight on g5 watches h7. On h8 the king no longer defends f8, and after 31...Kxh8, 32.Qxf8 is mate.
ex.at.eyGrj: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.at.eyGrj.hint: Look for the check that gives up a piece and pulls the black king away from the queen on e7.
ex.at.eyGrj.solution: 32.Re5+! The rook gives check, and every reply loses the queen. If 32...Kxe5, the king leaves the queen's side, and 33.Qxe7+ captures it with check. If the king goes to d7, d6 or f6, the rook on e5 defends e7, and the queen falls just the same.
part.advancedPawn.title: Advanced pawn
part.advancedPawn.summary: A pawn close to promoting forces the defence to give up material; sometimes the best is to promote to a knight.
ex.ap.oTiMh: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.ap.oTiMh.hint: Your pawn on a2 is one step from promoting. See which piece defends the promotion square.
ex.ap.oTiMh.solution: 35...a1=Q#! The pawn promotes with mate: the rook on a8 defends the new queen, and the white king has no free square.
ex.ap.t7Xii: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.ap.t7Xii.hint: Your pawn on g7 can capture the rook on f8. See which piece defends that square.
ex.ap.t7Xii.solution: 37.gxf8=Q#! The pawn captures the rook and promotes with mate: the bishop on d6 defends the new queen, and the black king has no free square.
ex.ap.b4WbR: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.ap.b4WbR.hint: Your pawn on c7 is one step from promoting. See which squares the black king still has.
ex.ap.b4WbR.solution: 55.c8=Q# The pawn promotes with check, and the black king has no free square: your king on d6 and the pawn on e6 watch d7, e7 and f7. Promoting to a rook also mates.
ex.ap.l3oYI: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.ap.l3oYI.hint: Your pawn on g2 can capture the rook on f1. See which squares the white king still has.
ex.ap.l3oYI.solution: 40...gxf1=Q# The pawn captures the rook and promotes with mate: the pawn on d3 watches c2 and e2, and the new queen, c1 and e1. Promoting to a rook also mates.
ex.ap.7hqXm: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.ap.7hqXm.hint: The rook on b1 guards e1 and f1, the squares where your pawn on e2 would promote. See how to remove that guard.
ex.ap.7hqXm.solution: 35...Qf1+! The queen gives check, and only the rook on b1 can capture it. After 36.Rxf1, 36...exf1=Q# is mate: the pawn captures the rook and promotes.
ex.ap.kmglB: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.ap.kmglB.hint: See which promotion square the knight on c3 does not watch, and what happens if it captures the advancing pawn.
ex.ap.kmglB.solution: 46...a2! The pawn threatens to promote on a1, a square the knight on c3 does not watch. If 47.Nxa2, 47...bxa2, and the other pawn heads for a1. After 47.Kh2, 47...a1=Q.
ex.ap.Ds2Zc: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.ap.Ds2Zc.hint: Your pawn on f7 can capture the rook on e8. Before promoting, compare the pieces: see which one attacks the king and the queen.
ex.ap.Ds2Zc.solution: 24.fxe8=N+! The pawn captures the rook and promotes to a knight: it is check, and the knight on e8 also attacks the queen on c7. After 24...Kh6, 25.Nxc7.
ex.ap.8bzUq: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.ap.8bzUq.hint: The rook on a5 guards a8, the promotion square of your pawn on a7. Look for a check that takes it off the a-file.
ex.ap.8bzUq.solution: 47.Rb5+! The rook gives check along the fifth rank. If the king steps away, the rook captures the one on a5. After 47...Rxb5, the black rook has left the a-file, and 48.a8=Q promotes.
ex.ap.aX36X: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.ap.aX36X.hint: The knight on e2 and the rook on e1 guard c1, the promotion square of your pawn on c2. Look for the move that removes both.
ex.ap.aX36X.solution: 26...Rxe2! The rook captures the knight that guarded c1. After 27.Rxe2, the white rook has left the first rank, and 27...c1=Q+ promotes with check.
